# A package-level initializer that contains a vectorizable loop must not break
# the build: rewriting it would leave simd calls in the generated package
# initializer, which fails at link time. Only the function's loop is rewritten.

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=example.com/app/vec
exec go build -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o app .
! stdout .
! stderr .
cmp log log.want

exec ./app
cmp stdout want.out

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
-- vec/vec.go --
package vec

var Spaces = func() string {
	b := make([]byte, 5)
	for i := range b {
		b[i] = ' '
	}
	return string(b)
}()

func Xor(x byte, b []byte) {
	for i := range b {
		b[i] ^= x
	}
}
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/vec"
)

func main() {
	b := []byte("hello, vectors and tails")
	vec.Xor(1, b)
	fmt.Printf("%q %q\n", vec.Spaces, b)
}
-- want.out --
"     " "idmmn-!wdbunsr!`oe!u`hmr"
-- log.want --
rewrote 1 loop(s) in example.com/app/vec
